text:
Montreal played the better game by almost every measure and lost 5-2. The Canadiens attempted 65 shots to Nashville's 45, controlled even-strength play 3.36 expected goals to 0.83, and would have won 78 percent of simulated replays. What decided it was a stretch of 1 minute and 50 seconds in the third period, when the Predators scored three times.

Nick Suzuki and Alex Newhook gave MTL a 2-0 lead in the second period, but Alexander Kerfoot's tip-in and a Matthew Wood power-play goal with 32 seconds left in the period tied it. The game turned on special teams from there. MTL took 20 penalty minutes to NSH's 6, and the Predators converted two of their five power plays. Ryan O'Reilly's tip-in at 16:44 of the third put NSH ahead.

Adam Edstrom then scored twice in 71 seconds, on chances the model rated at 84 and 63 percent, to turn a one-goal lead into a rout. Juuse Saros was the other difference, saving 1.7 goals more than his 33 shots deserved, including a 25 percent look from Josh Anderson in the third. Jacob Fowler allowed three goals on 18 shots and finished 1.03 goals below expectation.
